en: The Ritual for Repentance and Prostration Based on Various Sutras, Volume One,
compiled by the Śramaṇa Zhisheng of Xichongfu Monastery during the Great Tang Dynasty.
With all reverence, I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem.
All these people knelt with their right knees on the ground and,
holding incense and flowers, made offerings according to the Dharma,
making this aspiration: "May these clouds of incense and flowers..."
Pervading the realms of the ten directions,
they make offerings to all Buddhas,
as well as to emanation Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Countless assemblies of śrāvakas receive these clouds of fragrant flowers and use them as luminous pedestals.
Extending throughout boundless realms,
they perform buddha-activities within infinite and immeasurable buddha-fields;
they make offerings to all with reverence, uphold incense and flowers, practice the Way according to the Dharma, and universally recite [the scriptures].
The Tathāgata’s wondrous form-body is peerless in the world;
it is incomparable and inconceivable. Therefore, I now pay homage to the Tathāgata, whose form is inexhaustible and whose wisdom is likewise so.
All phenomena are eternally abiding; therefore, I take refuge in and pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem.

I praise the Buddha and offer prayers of aspiration. I praise the Buddha and offer prayers of aspiration: Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.
The Buddha possesses such immeasurable merit that it cannot be fully extolled. By means of these roots of goodness—
those already accumulated, those yet to be accumulated, and those currently being accumulated— [may all beings attain enlightenment].
By means of these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings in the Dharma-realm be nourished and benefited,
so that they may all attain liberation from suffering,
abandon what is false, and return to what is correct.
One generates the bodhicitta,
forever eliminates the three obstacles,
and constantly beholds all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and spiritual friends.
May we constantly hear the True Dharma and, endowed with merit and wisdom, attain Buddhahood simultaneously.

Homage to all Buddhas, such as the Tathāgata Sumerudīpaprabha in the eastern direction and all other Buddhas of the ten directions. Homage to all Buddhas, such as the Tathāgata Vipaśyin and the seven Buddhas of the past. Homage to all Buddhas, such as the Tathāgata Samantaprabha and the fifty-three Buddhas. Homage to all Buddhas, such as the Tathāgata Bhadraśrī in the eastern direction and all other Buddhas of the ten directions. Homage to all Buddhas, such as the Tathāgata Kanakamuni and the thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa. Homage to all Buddhas, such as the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and the thirty-five Buddhas. Homage to all Buddhas, such as the Tathāgata Akṣobhya in the eastern direction and the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions. Homage to the Buddha Ratnasaṃbhava.
Homage to the Buddha Ratnottama.
Homage to the Buddha Vairocanasiddha. Homage to the Buddha Vairocana-bimba. Homage to the Buddha Vairocana-prabha. Homage to the Buddha Akṣobhya.
Homage to the Buddha Mahāprabha.

Homage to the Tathāgata Immeasurable Sound. (Recite three times: Homage to the Tathāgata Immeasurable Sound; homage to the Tathāgata Immeasurable Sound. Homage to the Buddha Amitaghoṣa; homage to the Buddha Mahāyaśas;
homage to the Buddha Ratnaprabha;
homage to the Buddha Mahābhayaviharin; homage to the Buddha Dīpaṃkara.
Homage to the Buddha Real Sound.
Homage to the Buddha Boundless Stainless. Homage to the Buddha Moon Sound.
Homage to the Buddha Boundless Renown.

Homage to the World-Honored One, Radiance of Sun and Moon. (Recite three times) Homage to the World-Honored One, Radiance of Sun and Moon. Homage to the World-Honored One, Radiance of Sun and Moon. Homage to the Buddha Vimalaprabha. Homage to the Buddha Viśuddhaprabha.
Homage to the Buddha Sūryaprabha. Homage to the Buddha Anantaratna. Homage to the Buddha Puṣpavijaya.

Homage to the Buddha of Wondrous Body. Homage to the Buddha of Dharma-Radiance, Pure and Fully Blossomed Lotus. Homage to the Tathāgata King of Unobstructed Birth in the Dharma Realm, Adorned with the Transformation of Infinite and Boundless Sun and Moon Radiance and Vow-Power, Adorned with Various Ornaments, Crest-Jewel, and Fragrant Body of Lapis Lazuli Light, Supreme Fragrance, and Offerings Concluded; whose eyes are as pure as the atoms of space, whose features are upright and virtuous, and who is radiant with the light of flowers. Homage to the Tathāgata King of Marks, whose ūrṇā-kośa is like the radiance of the sun and moon, whose body is firm as diamond, adorned with precious lotus flowers, and who is Vairocana with unobstructed eyes that fill the ten directions and emit light illuminating all Buddha-fields. [This is] universally for the sake of the four debts of gratitude, the three realms of existence, and all sentient beings of the dharma realm.
To sever the three obstructions, I take refuge and repent. Thus, throughout all such worlds,
the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, eternally abide in the world.
May all these World-Honored Ones look upon me with compassion and keep me in their mindful recollection.
May you bear witness for me:
whether in this life or in my previous lives.
Since beginningless saṃsāra, whatever various transgressions have been committed—
whether performed by oneself, or...
If one instructs another to perform it,
or sees them performing it and rejoices in it—
whether it be for a stūpa or for the Saṃgha.
If one takes property belonging to the Sangha of the four directions,
whether taking it oneself or instructing another to take it.
If one rejoices in the grasping at views,
or commits the grave crimes of the five immediate transgressions,
whether by doing so oneself;
If one causes others to commit them,
or rejoices in seeing them committed—
these constitute the ten unwholesome paths of action.
Whether committed by oneself, taught to others, witnessed being committed with rejoicing,
or whether the various sins committed were concealed or not concealed—
one should fall into the hells, the realm of hungry ghosts, the animal realm, or other evil destinies, such as the borderlands, the lowly classes, and the Mlecchas.
I now repent of all such karmic obstructions created in these and other places.
Now, O Buddhas, World-Honored Ones...
"You should bear witness to me and remember me.
Furthermore, before all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones,
I shall speak these words:"
Whether in this life or in other lives,
I have ever practiced giving.
Whether it be maintaining pure precepts,
or even giving a single morsel of food to an animal,
or cultivating pure conduct— all such roots of goodness.
All roots of goodness for maturing sentient beings;
all roots of goodness for practicing bodhi;
and all roots of goodness for seeking unsurpassed wisdom.
Having gathered, calculated, and deliberated upon all [merits],
they dedicate them entirely toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*,
just as the Buddhas of the past, future, and present have dedicated their own.
I likewise dedicate in this way:
I repent of all transgressions; I rejoice in all merits and invoke the merit of the Buddhas, wishing that supreme wisdom may be attained.
To the Buddhas of the past, future, and present, The most supreme among sentient beings, oceans of immeasurable merit— I take refuge and pay homage with palms joined;
Recite this universally, recite this universally: Namo Mahāprajñāpāramitā.
This is a great divine spell;
this is a great illuminating spell;
this is an unsurpassed spell.
This is the peerless mantra.
Abiding in the world like space, like a lotus flower that is not defiled by water,
with a mind pure and transcending all that— homage is paid to the Unsurpassed Honored One.
May these merits be universally extended to all; may we and all sentient beings together attain the path to Buddhahood.
Having thus paid homage to the Buddha with reverence.
Taking refuge in the Buddha, may all beings realize the Great Way and give rise to the supreme aspiration.
Taking refuge in the Dharma, may all beings enter deeply into the treasury of the scriptures, their wisdom becoming like [the Dharma].
Taking refuge in the Sangha, may all beings lead and govern the great assembly, free from all [hindrances].
I entreat you all to listen as I recite the verses on impermanence at dusk: "Today has already passed;
the night ahead cannot be relied upon. Behold this body!"
Moment by moment one grows old;
a hundred years is the constant limit.
How can this be guaranteed?
Therefore, you all should diligently practice the Path with a focused mind:
all conditioned phenomena are impermanent.
These are phenomena subject to arising and ceasing.
When arising and ceasing have ceased,
extinction is bliss.
The Tathāgata has realized nirvāṇa and forever severed birth and death;
if one can listen with a sincere heart, [one shall likewise attain it].
One shall always obtain immeasurable bliss.
*The Scripture on the Names of the Buddhas of the Ten Directions*, one fascicle. With all reverence, I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem.
The wondrous form-body of the Tathāgata— In all the world, there is none equal to it.
Incomparable and inconceivable, Therefore I now pay homage to the Tathāgata.
The form [of the Buddha] is inexhaustible, And wisdom is likewise so;
All phenomena are eternally abiding, Therefore I take refuge in you.
Homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem.
In the heavens above and the earth below, none is equal to the Buddha; Throughout the worlds of the ten directions, there is likewise no peer.
I have beheld all that exists within these worlds, And find that none at all is like the Buddha.
Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha. Homage to the future Honored Buddha Maitreya. Homage to all Buddhas, the Tathāgatas of Good Virtue in the eastern direction.
Homage to all Buddhas, the Tathāgatas of Unsurpassed Virtue in the southeastern direction.
Homage to all Buddhas, the Tathāgatas of Sandalwood Merit in the southern direction. Homage to [all Buddhas] in the southwestern direction.
All Buddhas pay homage to Tathāgata Ratnadatta. All Buddhas pay homage to Tathāgata Amitābha in the western direction.
All Buddhas pay homage to Tathāgata Kusumaśrī in the northwest. All Buddhas pay homage to Tathāgata Lakṣaṇaśrī in the northern direction.
All Buddhas pay homage to Tathāgata Triyānacara in the northeast. All Buddhas [pay homage].
Homage to all Buddhas of the Tathāgata Viśvaguṇarāja of the upper direction; homage to all Buddhas of the Tathāgata Guṇarāja of the lower direction;
homage to the thousand Buddhas and fifteen hundred Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa; homage to the five hundred Puṣpottama and ten billion Vajragarbha Buddhas;
homage to the thirty-five Buddhas and fifty-three Buddhas; homage to those who have passed beyond.
I pay homage to the śarīras, images, stūpas, and temples of all Buddhas of the past, present, and future;
I pay homage to the twelve divisions of the honored scriptures, the profound treasury of Dharma; I pay homage to all the great bodhisattvas and all worthy sages;
and I pay homage to the lords of the twenty-eight heavens, including Śakra and Brahmā.
By taking refuge in the eternally abiding Triple Gem, may the winds and rains be timely for all dragons, spirits, and others.
By paying homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem, may the teachers of the past and present always serve as our guides and leaders.
I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem for the sake of the Emperor and Empress, that their sacred transformation may be infinite.
I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem for the sake of all kings, princesses, civil and military officials, and the hundred functionaries.
I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem for my currently living parents and all spiritual friends.
I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem so that patrons throughout the ten directions may bring the six perfections to fulfillment.
I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem for the sake of all humans and spirits of this land who have passed away, so that they may be reborn in the Pure Land.
I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem for the sake of the monastery deity and their retinue.
I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem for the sake of peace in the four directions and the laying down of weapons.
I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem for the sake of sentient beings suffering in the three miserable realms and the eight difficult conditions.
I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem; for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, to forever eliminate the three obstructions, I take refuge and repent.
The Buddhas of the ten directions are infinite, There is nothing they do not know;
Before them all, I now confess All my dark and evil deeds— The nine types, formed by three times three, Arisen from the three afflictions, In this present life...

If in previous lives I have committed any offenses, I now repent them all. Should there be karmic retribution to be endured within the three evil realms, may I instead repay it with this present body, rather than entering those evil paths to suffer.
Having finished the confession,
I take refuge and pay homage to the Triple Gem.
To all the Buddhas of the ten directions who have currently attained enlightenment, I entreat you to turn the wheel of Dharma for the sake of peace.
To all the Buddhas of the ten directions who delight in the welfare of sentient beings— if they wish to relinquish their life-span—
I now prostrate with my head at their feet, entreating them to remain for a long time.
Having made this request,
one takes refuge in and pays homage to the Triple Gem.
Whatever merit there is from acts of giving, from maintaining the precepts, and from the practice of meditation— all arising from body, speech, and mind— [I dedicate it] for the sake of [all beings].
All those of the present who practice the three vehicles, Those who are fully endowed with the three vehicles,
And the merit of all ordinary beings— May the assembly rejoice in it all.
Having rejoiced, I take refuge and pay homage to the Triple Gem.
May all the merit I possess be gathered together for the sake of all sentient beings. Rightly...
Dedicate it toward the Buddha-way.
Having dedicated it,
take refuge and pay homage to the Triple Gem.
May all sentient beings alike Awaken the bodhicitta; Binding their minds in constant mindfulness, May they contemplate all Buddhas of the ten directions.
Furthermore, may all sentient beings Permanently shatter all afflictions And clearly perceive the Buddha-nature, Just like Samantabhadra and others.
Having made this vow,
I take refuge in and pay homage to the Triple Gem and all the Great Virtuous Ones.
Seeking the bliss of tranquility,
one should train in the dharma of a śramaṇa;
regarding food and clothing, one should consider only the sustenance of the body, accepting whether it be coarse or refined, in accordance with the community.
This morning, on such-and-such a day, the monks each performed the six recollections.
Having completed the six recollections, they paid homage to the Buddha with reverence.
I take refuge in the Buddha; May all sentient beings realize and understand the Great Way, And give rise to the unsurpassed resolve.
Taking refuge in the Dharma, may all beings penetrate deeply into the treasury of the sutras.
Taking refuge in the Sangha, may all beings govern the great assemblies.
May all sentient beings be free from all worldly desires, purify their three karmas, uphold the sublime teachings, and pay homage to the Noble Ones.
The Dharani of the Mahāsannipāta Sūtra: Homage to the Buddha! Hu lu lu, si du lu, che fu po, qi li po, xi tan ni, bu lu ni, svāhā. This dharani is extracted from the Mahāsannipāta Sūtra.
Reciting this once is equivalent to reciting all twelve divisions of the scriptures once.
Furthermore, one should perform prostrations to the names of fifteen thousand Buddhas forty-eight thousand five hundred times.
Moreover, the person who maintains this mantra shall become like the dust motes upon the great earth.
May all such sins as these be universally extinguished.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, Savior from Suffering.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, Savior from Suffering.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, Savior from Suffering.
The merit of the ten recitations chanted thus far,
and these vast roots of goodness, shall provide benefit and sustenance for the deceased.
Flower terraces and flower pavilions welcome one from within the void;
precious thrones and jeweled beds receive one through the air.
Within the mani palace, one hears the teachings on suffering and emptiness.
In the pool of Prajñā, one washes away the defilements of the mind;
Avalokiteśvara and his manifested Buddhas act as witnesses;
and before Maitreya, one clearly receives the prediction of enlightenment.
The six classes of kinsmen and seven generations of ancestors shall find their causal conditions fulfilled;
adorned with a hundred merits, they shall be protected by devas and nāgas,
and the sufferings of the three evil realms shall be stilled.
The bitterness in hell ceases;
the great beings and the deceased alike are simultaneously freed from suffering.
Homage to the Noble Assembly.
Dāna is the foremost of the ten thousand practices;
by relinquishing attachment and abandoning stinginess and greed,
one becomes a donor in this present life.
Holding wealth to offer as alms—
with these supreme roots of goodness,
the karmic fruit will be inexhaustible.
Reaching even those suffering sentient beings,
they shall attain the path of Buddhahood in the future.
Maintaining pure precepts as prescribed, they respectfully offer porridge at the appropriate times.

Ten benefits bring great profit to the practitioner: physical strength, vitality, longevity, happiness, eloquence in speech, the clearing of undigested food and wind-disorders, and the elimination of hunger and thirst. This is called the "Excellent Medicine" taught by the Buddha.
Those who wish to be born in heaven and enjoy long-lasting bliss should offer rice gruel to the Sangha.
Homage to all Buddhas of the ten directions—past, future, and present—who are boundless; whose wisdom of true suchness is equal to space and immovable;
whose pure, luminous consciousness is the *amala-vijñāna*; whose pure Dharma-body is the *vairocana*;
whose perfect reward-body is the *lokeśvara*; and who manifest thousands of millions of transformation bodies.
Śākyamuni appears in this Sahā world; the essence of the three Buddhas is identical to that of all others.
Therefore, I prostrate to all the Buddhas—Namo to the infinite ones of the ten directions!
To all Buddhas of the past, future, and present, whose bodies are like a freshly polished mirror, and whose minds are as pure as mani jewels—to all these Buddhas...
All enter into my body, and I likewise enter the bodies of all Buddhas; we penetrate one another like reflections in a mirror.
Without coming or going, our essence is empty and void; unobstructed and unimpeded, there is neither birth nor cessation.
Therefore, I prostrate to the True Suchness of the Mind. Homage to those of the ten directions, boundless and limitless—past, future, and present.
The true bodies of all Buddhas are like mirrors; the true bodily forms of noble ones and ordinary beings are clearly manifest.
Each individual body manifests all bodies, and within every body, there are infinite bodies. The nature of phenomena is pure, its essence empty and fused;
these bodily forms interpenetrate without obstruction, as the Dharma-body is perfectly complete and pervasive throughout all phenomena.
Because of the *dhātu*, I prostrate to the Tathāgatagarbha. Homage to all Buddhas of the ten directions—past, future, and present—whose mind-nature as noble and ordinary beings is the Tathāgata.
Possessing the wealth of all meritorious qualities, the light of their wisdom constantly shines everywhere; the naturally pure mind is primordially open and eternal.
Blissful, self, pure, true consciousness and wisdom, Pure, unchanging, and luminous from beginning to end;
Having long traversed the path of suchness to achieve perfect enlightenment, I therefore prostrate to the Tathāgata Mind.
Homage to all Buddhas of the ten directions— Boundless, past, future, and present— The wisdom of the true suchness of the Dharma-body’s real mark, Serene and perfectly complete.
Pervading the entire world is the dhāraṇī of all treasuries of the Dharma; this dhāraṇī is the mind capable of making excellent vows.
It is not seen, heard, or cognized through faith; it is without knowledge, view, or cognition, yet it is the true awakening.
Self-awakened and awakening others, the Buddha is non-dual. Therefore, I prostrate to the Buddha-nature of the body. Namo to the Buddhas of the ten directions!
The Ultimate Limit: All Buddhas of the past, future, and present possess the true, correct path and a heart of great compassion.

Their intrinsic nature is pure and profoundly deep; it is neither cultivated nor contrived, and cannot be attained through views. It transcends names and cuts off conceptualization, being beyond thought and inquiry.
It is not produced as existence or non-existence, subtle and difficult to perceive; no demons or heterodox teachers can [fathom it].
Inviolable, eternally abiding, perfect, and without increase or decrease— Therefore, I prostrate to the bodhicitta.
Homage to all Buddhas of the ten directions, boundless, Of the past, future, and present. The nature of both Buddhas and sentient beings is primordially pure;
From beginning to end it remains as it is, long and ever serene. Its pure and tranquil body is most subtle and profound; Its essence...
Its nature is without arising or ceasing, eternally peaceful; free from discrimination, it neither increases nor decreases.
All virtues are perfected, quiescent and without end; possessing the eight masteries, it is true, eternal bliss. Therefore, I prostrate to Great Nirvāṇa.
Homage to all Buddhas of the ten directions—past, future, and present—and to the minds of all noble ones and ordinary beings.
The nature is eternally suchness, devoid of right or wrong and free from all extremes. The essence of the three realms and six paths is quiescent;
there is only the ultimate truth of the emptiness of nature. It shines forth universally and is eternally tranquil.
To reveal this true suchness through words and metaphors, one must realize that all phenomena are without subject or object. Therefore, I prostrate to you.
Prajñā-jñāna, I take refuge in all Buddhas of the ten directions, past, future, and present, who are boundless.
The nature of mind of both sages and ordinary beings is empty and without cause; it universally illumines the boundless ten directions.
The tranquil essence of True Suchness (Tathatā) fills all of space; the profound reality (bhūtalakṣaṇa) pervades the entire Dharma-realm. All Buddhas...
Dharmadhātu, this dhāraṇī is the mind capable of excellent vows; there is not a single phenomenon that does not purify the mind.
Therefore, I prostrate to the one of great luminous wisdom. Homage to all Buddhas of the ten directions, boundless in extent—those of the past, future, and present.
The nature of the mind of both the noble and the ordinary is primordially true; its self-nature is pure beyond verbal expression.
Neither empty nor existent, without subject or object, yet it can also serve as the cause of all phenomena; it establishes and brings forth all dharmas.
Without subject, without object, and without an agent, it is quiescent yet constantly active, without increase or decrease.
Therefore, I prostrate to the Dharmatā-kāya. Homage to the boundless [Buddhas] of the ten directions, who have come and gone.
The nature of the mind of all Buddhas of the present—both noble and ordinary—is empty and quiescent in essence.
Long since free from the dark gloom of ignorance and delusion, it constantly burns the torches of natural precepts, concentration, and wisdom; it is the lamp of liberation-knowledge and insight.
The five aggregates are in harmonious union without conflict; the light of tranquility shines universally, devoid of love or hatred—the Dharma-body of fivefold attributes.
Ever pure, I therefore prostrate to the unconditioned Saṅgha. Homage to all Buddhas of the ten directions—boundless, past, future, and present.
The mind-nature of both sages and ordinary beings is free from name and form, yet it perceives the adornments of the marks of name and form;
the pure mind and the Dharma-body are one and the same, capable of perceiving all phenomena such as forms.
The nature, the wisdom-body, the dharma-body, and the reward-response body are identical; the form-body is non-dual, its essence empty and tranquil.
According to conditions, it manifests as all manner of bodies; therefore, I prostrate to all the worthy sages.

In this equal prostration, there is neither one who does not prostrate nor one who does not receive it; with a single prostration, it pervades all sentient beings, for they all assemble within the essence of true reality.
Everyone is urged to take refuge in the Buddha; The seeds of all demons are eliminated, and True Suchness is revealed in its equality. Seeing one's nature, there is no remainder;
everyone is urged to take refuge in the Dharma, Which opens the treasury of sutras as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Within the state of mind of total retention, there is neither going nor coming;
I universally entreat you to take refuge in the Sangha. Opening the Way, one enters like a flowing stream;
The divine light of non-contention manifests, And all together return to the vessel of Prajñā.
I universally repent for the offenses of all views within the six sense-faculties. In the past, I was deluded regarding the Truth and mistakenly grasped at it as real;
now I know that truth and falsehood have always been one. Birth-and-death and nirvana are causes of quiescence;
through penetrating the light of the Dharma, there is inward illumination. The wondrous marks of Bodhi transcend both distance and intimacy.
The Lion’s Roar of the King of Unobstructed Wisdom Shatters all afflictions into fine dust;
Within every single atom dwell infinite Buddhas, And each Buddha manifests boundless bodies.
Within them appear merits as numerous as the sands of the Ganges— The treasury of the mind of the Triple Gem in its entirety.
The True Pure Land is the equality of suchness; The ocean of diamond nature is profound with the light of wisdom.
I vow that all sentient beings may together realize this; I universally entreat you to open the mind and behold the Dharmakāya.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage To the Buddha of the Suchness-Dharmakāya.
May I, together with all sentient beings, Return as one to the ocean of True Suchness—
Without color and without form, Without root and without abode,
Because it is neither born nor extinguished; I pay homage to that which is beyond all observation.
Neither going nor staying, neither grasping nor abandoning;
because of being far removed from the six sense bases, I pay homage to the one who has nothing to observe and has transcended the three realms, equal to space itself.
Homage to you who are unstained by any desires;
Homage to you who are without focal point, remaining ever in tranquility amidst all modes of conduct— whether moving or staying, waking or sleeping.
Past and future are entirely equal; you abide in equality because you do not destroy equality.
I pay homage to you who have nothing to observe, who enter the concentration of signlessness, and who perceive all phenomena as tranquil.
Because they constantly enter into tranquility, I pay homage to the Buddhas who have no object of observation and whose nature is like space.
Since space itself has no characteristics and is free from all causes and effects, I pay homage to those who have no object of observation.
Space has neither center nor periphery, and the bodies of all Buddhas are likewise;
because the mind is identical to space, I pay homage to the Buddha who has nothing to observe,
who ever abides in the world yet remains unstained by worldly dharmas.
I pay homage to you who do not conceptualize the world;

I pay homage to you who have nothing to observe, for all phenomena are like illusions. Since they are like illusions and unattainable, and because you are free from all illusory phenomena, I pay homage to you who have nothing to observe.
With this equal offering of homage— wherein there is neither homage nor non-homage—
a single prostration encompasses all sentient beings. May we together realize the essence of the true nature (dharmatā) for the sake of the four debts of gratitude,
those in the three realms of existence, and all beings in the six destinies.
Severing the three obstacles,
they resolve to attain bodhicitta and take refuge through repentance.
We repent with a sincere heart.
Disciples, since beginningless time, we have been deluded regarding our fundamental nature and have pursued the emotions of ignorance.
Because of the false conception of body and mind,
the discrimination between self and other arises;
from this, evil karma is produced.
In vain one assumes the forms of the six realms;
though one observes and seeks their master, the true source is nowhere to be seen.
It is an ocean of the three poisons: greed, hatred, and delusion.
Truth is Nirvana. Today I repent of my own accord;
henceforth, I shall no longer indulge my passions.
The myriad sins of ten million kalpas are dissolved in a single thought-moment.
Having finished the repentance:
With a sincere heart, I take refuge in and pay homage to the Triple Gem.
With a sincere heart, I entreat all the Great Compassionate Honored Ones of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
I only pray that you will abide forever and not enter nirvana;
sentient beings of the three realms are deluded and have not yet awakened—
how may they soon behold the true source?
Following the mind with the mind, one is unaware;
through false attachments and inversions, one sinks forever into samsara.
I only pray that the Compassionate Honored One will compassionately accept this request.
Having used various skillful means to lead all sentient beings and having exhorted them [to request the turning of the wheel of Dharma],
they take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Triple Gem,
rejoicing with a sincere heart.
Those who have already attained Buddhahood in the past are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges;
those who are currently practicing for the future [enlightenment] are likewise.
It causes the sprouts of bodhi to grow far and long.
The triple world has no fundamental basis;
it is like flowers in the sky.
I only pray that you will contemplate this deeply and enter into meditative absorption,
so that we may together roam through the Dharma-realm, the home of all Buddhas.
Having expressed my sympathetic joy, I say:
With a sincere heart, I take refuge in and pay homage to the Triple Gem.
With a sincere heart, I dedicate [this merit].
Since beginningless time, my mind has wandered in saṃsāra.
Never for a single thought-moment have I correctly dedicated [merit];
today I finally realize that the mind is unborn.
From the past until now, I was deluded and obscured, creating hindrances for myself.
May practitioners, like all Buddhas,
be free from conceptualization and discrimination as they perform right dedication. Having performed this dedication, [may they attain enlightenment].
With a sincere heart, I take refuge in and pay homage to the Triple Gem.
With a sincere heart, I make this vow:
may all sentient beings behold the source of the mind.
May we swiftly depart from afflictions and cross the ocean of suffering;
may we quickly realize the Great Nirvana within our own bodies.
We pray only that the Compassionate Honored One will grant his protective mindfulness.
Do not stagnate in the views of existence and non-existence;
having made this vow,
take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Triple Gem.
This refers to the formulation of the ten great vows based on the Avataṃsaka Sūtra.
As for the first vow: may the disciples and others...
Throughout all kalpas and in all places of birth,
they shall constantly revere and make offerings to all Buddhas,
without ceasing until the end of the future.
The second vow is:
May the disciples and others always receive and uphold the profound Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas, the Tathāgatas.
He immediately attained self-awakening without relying on the enlightenment of others,
continuing without rest until the end of the future.
This was his third vow.
May we, the disciples, always take the gathering of the Dharma as our foremost priority within the places where all Buddhas sit at the site of enlightenment.
I pray that you turn the Wheel of Dharma,
without ceasing until the end of the future.
This is the fourth vow.
May we, the disciples, always practice all the great vows and great deeds of the bodhisattvas,
without ceasing until the end of the future.
The fifth vow is: May the disciples and others always be able to teach and transform all sentient beings.
Whether born from an egg, born from a womb, born from moisture, or born by transformation;
whether possessing form or formless;
whether possessing perception or non-perception.
Whether they possess perception or are without perception,
I shall cause them all to enter nirvana without remainder.
In this way, I bring immeasurable and boundless sentient beings to parinirvāṇa.
In truth, there are no sentient beings who attain parinirvāṇa;
[this vow] shall continue without ceasing until the end of the future.
As for the sixth vow:
May we, the disciples,
always know all the buddha-fields as if they were before our very eyes,
without ceasing until the end of the future.
The seventh vow is:
May the disciples and others always be able to adorn and purify all Buddha-lands.
May it continue without rest until the end of the future.
As for the eighth vow: may the disciples and others...
They shall never be separated from all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and spiritual friends;
with one mind they shall practice and accumulate all roots of goodness,
without ceasing until the end of the future.
The ninth vow: May the disciples and others,
regarding all their three karmas, [be purified].
If there are sentient beings who see or hear [this],
none will pass by it in vain,
just like the great medicinal king-tree.
Like a wish-fulfilling jewel body,
it shall continue without rest until the end of the future.
As for the tenth vow:
May the disciple attain equal and perfect enlightenment and turn the Great Wheel of Dharma,
delivering and liberating all sentient beings without ceasing until the end of the future.
I vow that by means of these roots of goodness cultivated through prostrating to the Buddhas, practicing the Way, repenting, making vows, burning incense, and lighting lamps,
I shall dedicate them all for the benefit of all sentient beings.
May all sentient beings forever leave behind all places of suffering in the hells, the realm of hungry ghosts, the animal realm, and the domain of King Yama;
may they always be born among humans and devas, where they may behold the Buddhas and hear the Dharma.
They resolve to attain bodhicitta and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva.
Furthermore, they dedicate these roots of goodness toward unsurpassed enlightenment.
I do not seek the karmic fruits of birth and death within the mundane world.
Furthermore, I vow to dedicate these roots of goodness toward the ocean of the *tathatā* dharma-realm.
This is the text for praising the West and paying homage to Amitābha Buddha:
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.

Contemplate that realm of Amitābha’s Ultimate Bliss: vast, expansive, and level, composed of myriad jewels; adorned by the fulfillment of his forty-eight vows, it is the most sublime among all Buddha-fields. The great multitudes from this land and other quarters—whose names could not be known even by calculating for an entire kalpa—are universally exhorted to return to the West to join that assembly, where the sands-of-the-Ganges samādhis will be spontaneously perfected.
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.

The subterranean adornments are banners of the seven treasures, immeasurable, boundless, and beyond counting; formed of a hundred jewels across the eight directions and eight facets, seeing them, one realizes birthlessness spontaneously. The treasure-land of birthlessness is eternally constant; from each jewel flow countless rays of light, which the practitioner, with a devoted heart, gazes upon constantly, as their spirit soars and leaps into the Western Quarter.
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.

The adornments of the ground unfold infinitely; the paths demarcated by golden cords were not fashioned by craftsmen. Through the skillful adornment of Amitābha’s vows and wisdom, Bodhisattvas, humans, and devas scatter flowers upon them. From the jewel-pools, jewel-hued light radiates forth; from each ray of light, countless terraces arise. Within these terraces stand jeweled towers numbering in the thousands of millions, surrounded on all sides by billions of jeweled banners.
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.

Upon each and every terrace, within the void of space, the adornments of precious delights are likewise inexhaustible. Eight kinds of pure breezes emerge following the light, and at all times musical instruments are played, their sounds responding to the capacities of beings. Such responsive sounds are somewhat difficult to receive in meditative absorption; therefore, whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, one should maintain mindfulness and contemplation. Except for the time of eating, one should constantly keep this in mind: the unconditioned samādhi is itself nirvāṇa.
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.

In the Jewel Land, there are jewel groves and various jewel trees, with jewel flowers, jewel leaves, and jewel roots and trunks. Some forests are distinguished by being composed of a thousand jewels, while others are formed of a hundred jewels together. Row after row they face one another, and leaf follows leaf in succession; their colors are each different, and their radiance is likewise. They are all equal in measure, reaching thirty thousand [yojanas] in height; their branches touch one another, yet it is said to be without cause.
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.

Seven layers of jeweled nets and seven layers of palaces interlace and reflect light, shining brilliantly upon one another. Transformed celestial youths fill every space, their necklaces emitting a radiance that surpasses the sun and moon. Row after row of precious leaves display a thousand colors; the blooming flowers appear like the scattering of golden wheels. The vast transformations of light form myriad jeweled canopies, appearing boundlessly throughout Buddha-lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.

The jewel ponds with their jewel shores and golden sands, the jewel channels, jewel leaves, and jewel lotuses—twelve *yojanas* in perfect symmetry—are adorned with jewel pavilions, jewel nets, and jewel railings. The waters of virtue branch out along the jewel trees; hearing the waves and beholding the joy, one realizes tranquility. I address those with the karmic affinity to travel this path together: exert yourselves to overturn delusion and return to your original home.
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.

Upon every single path demarcated by golden cords, there are thousands of millions of precious jeweled trees and jeweled pavilions. Celestial youths scatter flowers and incense, while Bodhisattvas from other directions gather like clouds—immeasurable, boundless, and beyond calculation. They prostrate to Amitābha and stand in reverent attendance. The sound of wind-chimes and trees pervades the void, extolling the Three Honored Ones without end.
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.

The Flower-King Throne of Amitābha’s Original Vow is composed of every kind of precious jewel; upon its four-tiered dais, jeweled canopies are spread, where Amitābha sits alone, manifesting his true form. The radiance of this true form pervades the entire Dharma-realm; those touched by this light find their minds never regressing. By single-mindedly recollecting him throughout the six periods of day and night, at the end of life one will experience bliss as if in samādhi.
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.

Amitābha’s body and mind pervade the Dharma-realm, appearing as reflections within the thoughts of sentient beings. Therefore, I exhort you to constantly observe: by giving rise to images through the mind, behold his true countenance. That true countenance, a precious image, sits upon a lotus throne; when the mind opens, one beholds the splendors of that land. Precious trees abound with the three bodies and flowers, while wind-bells and music resound like the gates themselves.
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.

The body and color of Amitābha are like a mountain of gold; his marks and signs, and his radiance, illuminate the ten directions. Only those who practice mindfulness of the Buddha are gathered by his light; one should know that his original vow is most powerful. The Tathāgatas of the ten directions extend their tongues as witnesses: by single-mindedly reciting the Name, one reaches the Western Land. Upon arrival there, the flower blooms and one hears the wondrous Dharma; the vows and practices of the ten stages naturally manifest.
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.

Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, with great compassion, has fulfilled bodhi yet refrains from realizing it. Within the bodies of all beings throughout the five realms, he observes the three spheres during the six periods of the day. His manifested body is of purple-gold hue, and his marks, signs, and majestic deportment are infinitely transformative. He constantly extends the hands of the King of a Hundred Billion Radiant Lights, universally receiving those with karmic affinity and leading them back to the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.

The Bodhisattva Śrīkṣetra is inconceivable; his majestic radiance shines universally without limit. Sentient beings with whom he has a karmic affinity, touched by this light, increase their wisdom and transcend the three realms. The Dharma-realm trembles like a tumbleweed, and transformation Buddhas and Bodhisattvas fill the void. I universally exhort those with affinity to constantly mindfully recollect the Buddha, so that they may forever sever the womb-birth and realize the six supernormal powers.
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.

Sitting upright and binding the hands in the *samādhi* gesture, one contemplates the mind-vehicle of mindfulness reaching the Western Quarter. One beholds the realm of Amitābha’s Ultimate Bliss, with the earth and the void adorned with the seven treasures. The body of Amitābha is infinitely vast; yet he repeatedly exhorts sentient beings to contemplate his smaller form, manifesting as sixteen feet or eight feet according to their capacities. His halo transforms attendants who are equal in truth to those before him.
I vow that together with all sentient beings,
we shall be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.

Those of the highest rank, highest practice, and superior faculties who seek birth in the Pure Land sever greed and anger; according to the distinctions of their practice, they are divided into three grades. Through the five gates practiced continuously, they assist the three causes. Whether for one day or seven days, they apply themselves with single-minded diligence; at the end of their lives, they board the lotus pedestal and emerge from the six dusts. How joyful it is to encounter what is so difficult to meet! Thus they eternally realize the body of the unconditioned Dharma-nature.
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.

Those of middle capacity and middle faculties in the Middle Grade observe the precepts for one day and dwell upon golden lotuses. By filially supporting their parents and dedicating the merit toward rebirth, they are taught the causes for the happiness of the Western Land. The Buddha and his assembly of śrāvakas come to receive them, leading them directly before the flower-seat of Amitābha. After seven days within a cage of a hundred jewels, the three grades of lotuses open, and they realize the Lesser Truth.
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.

Those of the lower grade, with inferior conduct and dull faculties—those who commit the ten evil deeds and the five heinous crimes, driven by greed and anger; those who violate the four grave precepts, steal from the Sangha, or slander the True Dharma—who have never felt shame or remorse for their past transgressions—will find all manner of suffering gathering like clouds at the time of death. As the fierce fires of hell approach the sinner, they may suddenly encounter a spiritual friend who encourages them to single-mindedly recite the name of that Buddha. Transformation Buddhas and Bodhisattvas will arrive immediately upon hearing their voice; with a single thought of total devotion, the person enters a precious lotus. Though their heavy karmic obstructions from the three activities remain, they shall pass through many kalpas until, at that time, they finally give rise to the cause of Bodhicitta.
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.

What joy is there more inconceivable than this? Boundless Bodhisattvas are my fellow students; the Tathāgata Sea of Nature is my every teacher. Thirsting for the hearing of Prajñā, I have abandoned all thought of water; mindful of the food of non-arising, I am instantly freed from hunger. All adornments preach the Dharma; I receive it naturally without a mind to grasp. I enter the jeweled lotus ponds at will; the Eight Classes of Beings concentrate their spirits at a single branch. The water of Amitābha’s heart bathes my head and crown; Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta clothe me in robes. In an instant, I soar through space to roam the Dharma-realm; in a mere moment, I am granted the prediction of enlightenment, named "The Unconditioned. How could I not go to such a place of supreme ease in Sukhāvatī? When shall I wait no longer?
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.
Out of compassion, protect me and cause the seeds of the Dharma to grow; in this life and in future births, may the Buddha always sustain me.
May I do so together with all sentient beings.
May we be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, we take refuge and pay homage to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
May we, together with all sentient beings, [attain this].
May we be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, we take refuge and pay homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
May we, together with all sentient beings, [attain this].
May I be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to the assembly of pure great ocean-like bodhisattvas in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.

For the sake of my teachers, parents, spiritual friends, and all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, I sever the three obstacles so that we may together attain rebirth in the Land of Amitābha Buddha.
I take refuge and repent; I repent with a sincere heart.

I take refuge and repent before the Buddhas of the ten directions; may all roots of sin be extinguished. I now dedicate all the merit from my long-standing and recent cultivation of goodness as the cause for the peace and happiness of myself and others. May, at the time of death, all supreme conditions and sublime realms appear before me. May I behold the Great Compassionate Lord Amitābha, along with Avalokiteśvara, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, and the Honored Ones of the ten directions. Looking up to their divine radiance, may I receive their hands and, by the power of the Buddhas' vows, be reborn in that land. Having finished this repentance, dedication, and aspiration, I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha.
He spoke these verses.
Having spoken these verses,
he should further make a vow with both mind and speech.
May my disciples, at the time of their death,
have minds that are neither inverted nor confused.
The mind does not lose mindfulness;
body and mind are free from all suffering and pain,
and they experience bliss as if entering meditative absorption.
The assembly of sages appears before them.
By virtue of the Buddha’s original vow, they attain the highest grade of the highest birth in the land of Amitābha Buddha.
Having reached that land, they attained the six supernormal powers and returned to enter the worlds of the ten directions to rescue and gather in suffering sentient beings.
"As far as the reaches of empty space and the dharma-realm extend, so too shall my vows extend. Having thus made this vow, one should single-mindedly take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha.
If the assembly wishes to cultivate the practices for rebirth in the Western Land, they should sit alone during the first watch of the night and reflect deeply within themselves.

Do not say you shall dwell long in Jambudvīpa; there will surely come a day when impermanence strikes. Life is like a single candle in a gale, or like a flash of lightning from within a rock. To hear that one’s body is healthy and strong, yet fail to practice asceticism, is like digging for a well when already parched with thirst—there, water is hard to find.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.

Now I contemplate this body and see it is truly loathsome—a body of various impurities, a mere provisional name. Three hundred fragments of bone support one another; throughout the entire frame, where is there even a single atom of reality? One never tires of smearing the body with perfumes and powders, yet in the end it becomes dust beneath the earth. How could the blazing fires of affliction ever cease? They are ultimately the cause for wandering through the three miserable realms. I universally exhort the assembly at this place of practice: with a sincere heart, recite the Buddha’s name and enter the gate of truth.
I vow that together with all sentient beings, we shall be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss. Greed and anger are the six thieves, devoid of any reality;

deluded thoughts wander aimlessly through this foul body. Amidst dreams, one wanders in all directions; yet upon sudden awakening, all is silent, empty, and void. The four elements are impermanent and return to dust and soil; the soul and spirit scatter—where can they be found? What was acquired in life is used by others; in the afterlife, one receives nothing but paper and clay money. For this reason, the Buddha dwells in the Western Land; I urge you all with diligence to engrave these words in your hearts.
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.
I vow to be reborn in the Buddha-land;
may the holy assembly everywhere take note.
Having now received the Buddha's teaching in this life, I make this aspiration.
I dare not give rise to further doubt.
For one day or seven days, I shall focus my mind with single-minded diligence.
I will surely attain rebirth in the West among the flowers, where I shall fulfill my vows together with all sentient beings.
One may be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss;

yet in the Pure Land, there is joy beyond compare, while in hell, the retribution of suffering crowds together. Hearing a single word of evil, they do not spare their own lives; they refuse to seek the True Dharma with a sincere heart. Upon death, they fall into the eighteen hells of Avīci; when will their suffering in saṃsāra ever come to an end?
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
Return, come back!
One cannot remain in the realm of Māra;
having wandered through vast eons,
one has traversed all six paths of existence.
Everywhere there is nothing else;
one hears only the sounds of birth and death.
For the remainder of this life, [one must face this].
Entering that city of nirvāṇa,
I vow that together with all sentient beings,
we shall be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
Behold that realm of Amitābha’s Sukhāvatī:
vast, expansive, and level, a city of myriad jewels,
with rows of cloud-like flowers beyond counting.
For the sake of the virtuous beings of this land who,
amidst the five turbidities, wish to cultivate the ten wholesome deeds,
first and foremost, they should single-mindedly recite the Amitābha Sūtra.
Reciting the Buddha’s name with mind and mouth without weariness,
at the end of life the Bodhisattva will come in person to welcome them.
May all sentient beings [share in this].
May I be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the West.
Contemplate clearly that there is a land in the western direction.
In that land there is a Buddha named Amitābha,
who preaches the Dharma while seated for kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
universally severing all demons for the sake of the world.
Ascending the noble throne within the city of Sukhāvatī,
all the devas gather around and come to pay their respects;
there is a multitude of eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas.
I reverently hold flowers and fruits and scatter them over Sahā;
may I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
May it universally cause Brahmā, Śakra, the Four Heavenly Kings, the eight classes of beings including devas and nāgas,
sovereigns, lords of men, teachers, monks, parents, spiritual friends, and all sentient beings throughout the dharma realm,
to sever and eliminate the three obstructions.
May we all attain rebirth in the land of Amitābha Buddha; taking refuge, I repent.
When the Tathāgata realized nirvāṇa, he forever severed birth and death;
if one can listen with a sincere heart, they shall always obtain immeasurable bliss.
Homage to the Original Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha and all the Triple Gem.
I now prostrate with my head to the ground and,
dedicating this merit, pray to be reborn in the Land of Immeasurable Life.
Homage to all the Three Jewels within the lands as numerous as atoms throughout the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm across the ten directions and the three periods of time.
I now prostrate with my head to the ground and dedicate this merit toward rebirth in the Land of Immeasurable Life.
Homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
Because I vow to take refuge together with all sentient beings,
I prostrate my head in worship to those born in that land.
Homage to the Buddha of Immeasurable Light in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
Because I vow to take refuge together with all sentient beings,
I prostrate my head in worship to those born in that land.
Homage to the Buddha Boundless Light of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
Because I vow that all sentient beings together shall take refuge,
I prostrate my head in worship to those born in that land.
Homage to the Buddha Unobstructed Light of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
May all sentient beings together take refuge;
I prostrate with my head to those born in that land.
Homage to the Buddha Adversity-Free Light of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
May all sentient beings together take refuge;
I prostrate my head in worship to those born in that land.
Homage to the Buddha King of Radiant Flames in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
Because I vow that all sentient beings together shall take refuge,
I prostrate my head in worship to those born in that land.
Homage to the Buddha Pure Light of the Land of Utmost Bliss in the Western Quarter.
May all sentient beings together take refuge;
I prostrate my head in worship to those born in that land.
Homage to the Buddha Joyful Light of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
May all sentient beings together take refuge;
I prostrate my head to those born in that land.

Because I vow to take refuge together with all sentient beings,
I prostrate my head in worship to those born in that land.
Homage to the Buddha Inconceivable Light of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
Because I vow that all sentient beings together shall take refuge,
I prostrate myself to be born in that land.
Homage to the Buddha Unnameable Light of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
May all sentient beings together take refuge;
I prostrate my head to those born in that land.
Homage to the Buddha Surpassing the Light of the Sun and Moon in the Land of Ultimate Bliss in the Western Quarter.
Because I vow to take refuge together with all sentient beings,
I prostrate my head in worship to those born in that land.
Homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
Out of compassion, protect and shelter me,
and cause the seeds of the Dharma to increase.
In this world and in future lives, may the Buddha always sustain me; for the sake of all sentient beings, may we together take refuge.
Therefore, I prostrate with my head to those born in that land.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
Because I vow to take refuge together with all sentient beings,
I prostrate my head to those born in that land.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
Because I vow to take refuge together with all sentient beings,
I prostrate my head in worship to those born in that land.
Homage to all the honored Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas and the pure great ocean-like assembly in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
May we, together with all sentient beings, take refuge in them.

I prostrate to those born in that land, universally for the sake of the Brahmās, Śakras, and the Four Heavenly Kings of the upper realms; the eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas; kings, sovereigns, teachers, monks, parents, and spiritual friends; and all sentient beings throughout the dharma realm.
May all vows be fulfilled to sever the three obstacles and together attain rebirth in the land of Amitābha Buddha.
I take refuge and repent.
Homage to the Buddha Samantaprabha.
Homage to the Buddha Samantajñāna.

As stated in the *Amitābha Sūtra*,
one will certainly attain rebirth provided they first possess three mental states. What are these three?
The first is the mind of utmost sincerity.
This means that through the action of body, one prostrates before that Buddha;
and through the action of speech, one praises and extols that Buddha.
With mental karma focused on single-mindedly observing that Buddha,
one must ensure that all three types of karma are authentic; therefore,
this is called the mind of utmost sincerity.
The second is the profound mind;
that is to say, it is true faith.
It is the conviction that one's own self is an ordinary person possessed of afflictions, with meager roots of goodness.
One wanders through the three realms, unable to escape the burning house.
Now, by faith, one knows that through Amitābha’s original great vows,
as well as by reciting his name even ten times, one will certainly attain rebirth in the Pure Land.
Even for a single moment, there is no doubt;
therefore, it is called the "deep mind.
Third is the mind of dedication and aspiration.
All roots of goodness performed are entirely dedicated toward the aspiration for rebirth;
therefore, it is called the "mind of dedication and aspiration.
One who possesses these three minds will certainly attain rebirth.
If even a single thought of single-mindedness is lacking, one will not be born there;
this should be understood as it is fully explained in the *Amitāyurdhyāna Sūtra*.
Furthermore, as the *Vimalakīrtinirdeśa-ṭīkā* by Vasubandhu states:
If there are those who wish to be born in that land,
they should be encouraged to practice the five gates of mindfulness;
if these five gates are complete, one will certainly attain birth there.
What are the five? First is the gate of bodily action through prostration,
which consists of single-mindedly and with utmost devotion joining the palms in reverence.
Offer incense and flowers as an act of worship;

It is called the "Gate of Prostration" because it is not mixed with other forms of ritual;
second is the "Gate of Verbal Praise," which consists of single-mindedly recollecting and praising the physical marks and radiance of that Buddha.
Because it encompasses the radiance of the physical marks of all the noble assembly,
as well as the radiance of all the jewel-adornments within that land,
it is called the "Gate of Praise."
Third is the gateway of mental action through mindfulness and observation.
This refers to single-mindedly recollecting and contemplating the physical marks and radiance of that Buddha and all the holy assemblies, as well as the adornments of their lands.
As stated in the *Amitābha-sūtra*:
"Except for the time of sleep,
one should constantly recollect, constantly mind, constantly contemplate, and constantly observe this matter."
Therefore, it is called the gate of observation.
Fourth is the gate of making vows,
which means to focus the mind exclusively, whether by day or by night.
At all times and in all places,
whatever merit is produced through the three karmas and the four modes of deportment—
without distinction between the beginning, middle, or end.
One must all truly generate a vow from within the heart with the aspiration to be born in that land; therefore, this is called the Gate of Vow.
Fifth is the Gate of Dedication (*pariṇāmanā*), which refers to single-mindedly dedicating whatever roots of goodness one has performed oneself.
Furthermore, one should deeply rejoice in all the roots of goodness performed by those of the three vehicles and five paths,
including each and every saint and ordinary person, just as the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas rejoice.
I likewise rejoice in this manner.
By means of these roots of goodness from my rejoicing, as well as the roots of goodness I have myself performed,
I share them all with all sentient beings and dedicate them toward that land.
Therefore, it is called the Gate of Dedication (*pariṇāmanā-mukha*).
Furthermore, having reached that land and attained the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍ-abhijñā*),
one returns to the cycle of birth and death (*saṃsāra*) to teach and transform sentient beings.
To exhaustively reach the furthest limit of time with a mind never weary or satisfied,
continuing until the attainment of Buddhahood,

Once these five gates are complete, one will certainly attain rebirth.
Each gate is integrated with the three aforementioned mentalities;

One should know that these are all called true and real karma.
