With a sincere heart, I take refuge in and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.
That Honored One’s buddha-field is free from ill repute, and there is neither woman nor fear of the evil realms;
because all beings reverently honor that Honored One with wholehearted devotion, I prostrate my head in worship to Amitābha Buddha.
May I, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.
That Honored One’s sphere of immeasurable skillful means is such that there are no evil friends among the various realms of rebirth;
one is born there and never regresses until reaching Bodhi. Therefore, I prostrate to Amitābha Buddha, and vow to do so together with all sentient beings.
May they be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the West.
I shall now proclaim the virtues and deeds of that Honored One: his manifold merits are as boundless as the waters of the ocean.
Those who purify the roots of goodness they have performed, dedicating them for the sake of all sentient beings so that they may be born in that land—
may they, together with all sentient beings,
be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
May the seeds of the Dharma increase In this life and in future births. May the Buddha always sustain us;
Together with all sentient beings, We vow to be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.

With a sincere heart, we take refuge and pay homage To Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss. Together with all sentient beings, We vow to be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.

With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss; may I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Happiness.

With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to the assembly of pure bodhisattvas, as vast as a great ocean, in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss. May I, together with all sentient beings—including my teachers, parents, spiritual friends, and all beings throughout the dharma realm—be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
Severing the three obstacles, may we all equally attain rebirth in the land of Amitābha Buddha.
We take refuge and repent; we repent with a sincere heart.
Since receiving this body in the beginningless past,
they have constantly inflicted the ten unwholesome deeds upon sentient beings;
they have been unfilial toward their parents and slandered the Triple Gem.
They commit the five heinous and unwholesome karmas;
due to these various causes and conditions of sin,
they give rise to delusions and inversions that produce entanglements.
I shall have to undergo immeasurable suffering through birth and death;
I prostrate and repent, praying that it may be extinguished.
Having repented, I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha.
With a sincere heart, I entreat you:
O Buddhas, Greatly Compassionate and Unsurpassed Honored Ones,
who constantly illuminate the three realms with the wisdom of emptiness.
Sentient beings are blind and ignorant, never awakening;
they sink forever into the great ocean of suffering of birth and death.
To uproot all living beings and free them from every form of suffering—[I have come forth].
Exhort and entreat the Buddhas to remain forever and turn the wheel of Dharma.
Having made this exhortation, take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha.
With a sincere heart, rejoice in the merit of all beings.
Throughout kalpas past, they have harbored jealousy;
their pride and negligence arise from delusion.
They constantly use the poisonous fire of hatred to cause harm.
The roots of merit of wisdom and compassion were consumed by fire;
today, through reflection, I have finally awakened.
I shall arouse great diligence and a mind of sympathetic joy.
Having expressed sympathetic joy, one should with a sincere heart take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha,
and with a sincere heart dedicate the merit:
"Wandering within the three realms..."
Through delusion and craving, one enters the prison of the womb;
once born, one returns to old age and death,
sinking into the ocean of suffering.
I now cultivate this merit and dedicate it toward rebirth in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
Having performed this dedication, I take refuge and pay homage with a sincere heart to Amitābha Buddha.
With a sincere heart, I make this vow:
may I cast off this form within the womb and be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
May they swiftly behold Amitābha Buddha,
whose body is of boundless merit,
and pay homage to all the Tathāgatas.
The noble sages are likewise so;
having attained the power of the six supernormal knowledges,
they rescue and gather in suffering sentient beings.
"As far as the reaches of space and the dharma-realm extend, so too shall my vows.
Having made this vow, I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha; all else is the same as the aforementioned Dharma."
The Fourth: Based on the Vow of Bodhisattva Vasubandhu, twenty prostrations for the Liturgy of Worship and Adoration for Rebirth [in Sukhāvatī].
At the time of the final watch of the night, the ritual of worship and repentance is the same as before and after.
I take refuge in the Tathāgata Unobstructed Light throughout the ten directions; may I be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
Surpassing the paths of the three realms, ultimately like space, vast and without limit— may I,
together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
Born from supramundane roots of goodness, replete with pure radiance, like the orbs of the sun and moon reflected in a mirror.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss,
Perfectly adorned and magnificent, with stainless light blazing intensely, Radiant and pure, illuminating the world. May I,
together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
The ponds, streams, and springs are completely covered; A gentle breeze stirs the flowers and leaves, Their interlacing radiance swirling in confusion.
May all sentient beings together Be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
Beholding the ten directions without obstruction, The various trees display diverse hues of light, And jeweled railings encircle them on all sides.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
A net pervades the entirety of space, where various bells ring out melodious sounds, proclaiming the wondrous voice of the Dharma.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
The subtle and wondrous One heard throughout the ten directions— The Perfectly Awakened Amitābha, the Dharma King who dwells in excellence.
May I, together with all sentient beings, Be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss;
Born by transformation from the flowers of Perfect Awakening, Delighting in the flavor of the Buddha-Dharma, And taking dhyāna and samādhi as my food.

May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss, where we may enjoy happiness without interruption; within the realm of the roots of goodness of the Mahāyāna, may there be no names of reproach or disparagement.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
The seeds of the two vehicles do not arise; I shall fulfill all the aspirations and joys of sentient beings.

Together with all beings, may we be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss upon sublime, pure lotus pedestals, with the marks and signs of excellence radiating one fathom of light, and with a physical form that transcends all other living beings.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss,
the King of the Ocean of Pure Wisdom, who is like Sumeru, the King of Mountains,
supremely wondrous and unsurpassed. May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
Reverently circling and gazing up, raining down celestial music, flowers, garments, and offerings of exquisite incense and the like,
may I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss;
may we constantly turn the stainless wheel [of Dharma] at every thought-moment and at every instant, benefiting all living beings.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss;
Without any discriminating mind, may we be able to swiftly fulfill The great ocean-treasury of merit.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
May the seeds of the Dharma increase in this life and in future births; may the Buddha always sustain us.
Together with all sentient beings, we take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Land of Peace and Bliss in the West.

Together with all sentient beings, we take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of the Land of Peace and Bliss in the West. Together with all sentient beings, we take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta of the Land of Peace and Bliss in the West. Together with all sentient beings, we take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the assembly of all Bodhisattvas, that pure great ocean, of the Land of Peace and Bliss in the West. For the sake of our teachers, parents, spiritual friends, and all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, may we together with all beings be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
Having severed the three obstacles,
may we all equally attain rebirth in the Land of Amitābha Buddha.
We take refuge and repent.
Fifth, based on the *Vandanā-gāthā for Aspiring to Rebirth* by Dharma Master Yancong:
perform twenty-two prostrations.
At the time of rising at dawn, the ritual of repentance is the same as before and after.
The fruit of ultimate bliss is profound; Rare treasures form its ground, And various jewels intersperse the groves.
Flowers bloom in wondrous colors, Waves carry forth the sound of true reality. When shall I receive your reaching hand?
May I fulfill my heart’s desire for rebirth there, And together with all sentient beings, Be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
The vow for the Pure Land grows ever deeper; The golden cords form straight boundary paths. Beaded nets hang down like canopies, and in the groves, all forms seen are true forms;
All sounds heard are the sounds of the Dharma. Do not say that the Western Land is far away— One need only have a mind of ten recitations.
I vow that together with all sentient beings, We shall be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
The True One possesses pervasive emptiness and majesty; When appearing in the West, he manifests in a small form. Both are temporary manifestations according to the capacities of beings.
Like leaves and pearls reflecting one another, Sand and water together shine with clarity. If you wish to attain the fruit of non-arising, That land must necessarily be relied upon.
I vow that together with all sentient beings, We shall be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
The mudrā of the Treasure Hand is ever-present; earth and water both serve as mirrors. Fragrance and flowers alike form clouds;
through profound karma, one easily attains rebirth there. For those of shallow roots, it is truly difficult to hear.
May you surely dispel all doubts and transcend the common crowd. Vowing together with all sentient beings, may we be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
Within the light manifesting throughout the five realms, Compassion draws them in, never ceasing; Though people return, they are not yet exhausted.
The mouth continues its proclamation while remaining in meditative concentration, And the mind, tranquil, further flies through supernatural powers. All who hear the name aspire to be reborn;
In days past, many clusters of flowers were offered. I vow that together with all sentient beings, We shall be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
The body’s radiance is fully endowed with conditions, Causing all jeweled lands to tremble. Those sitting in attendance on the golden lotus are not merely flocks of birds;
Those of celestial class are not truly gods. One must know that seeking sublime bliss depends entirely upon the fragrance of precepts.
I vow to dwell together with all sentient beings In the Land of Peace and Bliss.
The light encompasses the Dharma-realm in its perfection; Without conditions, it is able to gather all beings. When the meditative absorption arises, the flowers do not obstruct;
They transform according to one's original mind. The palace shifts, yet the body remains naturally at ease.
One who longs to hear of the supramundane realm must enter dhyāna together to behold it. May I, along with all sentient beings, Be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
The road to the West is gradually opening; Jeweled banners support the vast earth. Celestial incense enters the distant breeze;
Blossoms unfold, layered upon the waters. Fine nets cover and divide the void. How earnest is my wish to be reborn there, Seeking only infinite bliss!
I vow that together with all sentient beings, We shall be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
The West is the most worthy of refuge; Amidst the trees, multi-storied pavilions open. Fresh garments line the paths, and fragrant food arrives according to one’s heart’s desire;
Jeweled palaces fly after one’s person. All who have the karmic affinity may enter, yet those who go there are rare.
I vow that together with all sentient beings, We shall be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
He strictly purifies his realm to guide the multitudes of sentient beings; Golden sands shine through the waters, and jade leaves fill the branches.
Bright birds emerge from within pearls; Humans are born only atop lotus flowers. I venture to request that the Sage of the Western Land Will surely come to welcome me at dawn or dusk.
I vow to go together with all sentient beings To be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.

All are members of the Dharma King’s family; Seeking specifically those with whom there is a karmic affinity, I hope to attain early on the water of the eight merits that accords with one's wishes, And the natural blossoms of the seven treasures.
If one can fix the mind upon him, one will surely go there without delay. Vowing together with all sentient beings, May we be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
The ancient and the modern stand as one; The light-pavilion is joined with a thousand jewels.
Music proclaims the eight winds; in the pond dwell many birds preaching the Dharma. Heavenly beings fill the void, scattering flowers; Having attained birth there, they fear no regression.
May I, together with all sentient beings, Aspire to be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
The noble assembly is likewise immeasurable; The lotus blooms as one dwells alone. Waves arise as the Dharma naturally unfolds;
Freedom from calamity comes through abiding in stillness. Not retreating is the excellence of a true companion. I ask those of former lives:
how many kalpas have you endured to reach this place? May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
The Queen stands waiting for Vaidehī; The devas arrive, holding fragrant canopies. As people depart, they carry away precious robes;
At the six periods of the day, flocks of birds harmonize their songs. With every step of four inches upon the flowers, they bow low;
Beholding one another, all are upright—how could there be any further long delusion? I vow that together with all sentient beings, We shall be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
May all extinguish the five fires; The merit of generating the bodhicitta has already reached them. When mindfulness is maintained, transgressions are instantly eliminated.
Birds transform, pearl-light rotates, The breeze is pleasant and the sound of music is harmonious. All rejoice that practicing the Path is easy; why worry that the fruit of sainthood is remote?
I vow that together with all sentient beings, We shall be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
The golden light is the pedestal; when the time comes, the flowers scatter of their own accord.
Following one's vows, the petals open again as they move through the pond, appearing and disappearing. Flying through the air, they come and go in mutual exchange.
If one can direct the true mind toward that realm and cultivate merit together with all sentient beings, may we all be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.

Clouds of exquisite flowers that delight the eye; The mechanism of simultaneous birth is easily recognized. Lifespans are equal and difficult to distinguish; In bliss, there is no cessation of the Way.
Sounds travel far without hindering their hearing. How can one greedily cling to the five turbidities, Only to be calmly consumed by the fires of self-destruction?
I vow that together with all sentient beings, We shall be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
The attendant gazes within the light upon a four-jeweled pavilion suspended in mid-air; Its sevenfold railings overlook the vast expanse, yet one may doubt whether the land is truly eternal.
If virtue is meager, rebirth there is difficult; for now, let us set aside other vows.
Gazing westward, my heart is already at peace: I vow that together with all sentient beings, We shall be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
The three evil realms are forever severed; in a single thought-moment, one travels everywhere. Upon returning, the attainment of patience is perfected;
the earth is level, boundless, and vast. The winds are long-lasting and pure in this place.
I address those with resolve: together let us emerge from this perilous city. May we, along with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
May the seeds of the Dharma increase in this life and in future births. May the Buddha always sustain us;
may we, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss. With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage.

To Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss— may we, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss. With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage. To Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss— may we, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss. With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage. To the assembly of all Bodhisattvas in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, the pure ocean-like multitude—may we, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss. May it universally serve to sever the three obstructions for teachers, parents, spiritual friends, and all beings throughout the Dharma realm.
We shall together attain rebirth in the Land of Amitābha Buddha.
Taking refuge, we repent.
Sixth, the Bhikṣu Shandao’s *Vow for Rebirth* and *Verses of Liturgy and Praise* prescribe twenty prostrations based on the Sixteen Contemplations.
At midday, perform the ritual of repentance as prescribed for the preceding and succeeding periods.
With a sincere heart, take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.
Contemplate that realm of Amitābha, the Land of Ultimate Bliss, vast, expansive, and composed of myriad jewels.
Adorned by the arising of the forty-eight vows, it surpasses all Buddha-lands as the most sublime essence.
From the great ocean-like assemblies of this land and other directions, even if one were to calculate for an entire kalpa, their names could not be known.
Universally exhorting all to return to the West and join that assembly, the sands-of-the-Ganges samādhis will be spontaneously perfected.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.
The ground below is adorned with banners of the seven treasures, immeasurable, boundless, and beyond counting.
The eight directions and eight facets are composed of a hundred jewels; Beholding that state of non-arising, one spontaneously awakens to non-arising.
This jewel-land is eternally constant; From each jewel flow forth countless rays of light.
The practitioner inclines the heart and gazes constantly upon them; With spirit soaring and leaping for joy, they enter the Western Land.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.
The adornments upon the ground are infinitely wondrous; the paths demarcated by golden cords were not fashioned by craftsmen.
Adorned with the skillful wisdom of Amitābha’s vows, The ground is strewn with flowers by bodhisattvas, humans, and devas;
It is beautified by jewel colors and jewel lights, Each light forming countless tiers,
Within each tier are thousands of millions of jewel pavilions, Surrounded on every side by ten billion jeweled banners.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.
Upon each and every lotus pedestal in the void, the adornments of precious delights are likewise inexhaustible.
The eight kinds of pure breezes seek out the light; At all times, drums and music resonate with the sounds of the occasion.

These sounds of the occasion lead to right reception, though this is somewhat difficult. Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, one should maintain mindfulness by gathering the mind in contemplation.
Except during sleep, one should constantly maintain recollection; This unconditioned samādhi is itself nirvāṇa.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the West.
His precious land, his precious groves, and his various precious trees, with their precious flowers, precious leaves, and precious roots and trunks.
Some forests are distinguished by a thousand jewels, while others are composed of a hundred jewels;

their rows stand facing one another and their leaves follow in succession. Their colors are each different, as are their lights, yet they are equal in measure and height, reaching three hundred thousand [yojanas]. When the branches touch one another, they proclaim the causes and conditions.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.
Seven layers of jeweled nets and seven layers of palaces interlace and reflect one another’s radiance, shining forth in mutual brilliance.
Transformed celestial youths fill every place, Their necklaces radiating light surpassing the sun and moon.
Row upon row of jeweled leaves display a thousand colors; Blossoms unfold like revolving golden wheels.
The fruits transform their light into myriad jeweled canopies, Manifesting boundlessly across buddha-lands as numerous as motes of dust.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.
With jeweled ponds, jeweled shores, and jeweled golden sands; with jeweled channels, jeweled leaves, and jeweled lotus flowers.
Twelve *yojanas* all perfectly equal, with jewel pavilions, jewel nets, and jewel railings;
the waters of the *Śītā* river branch out, following the paths of the jewel trees. Hearing the waves and beholding the joy, one realizes tranquility.
Send word to those with the karmic affinity and those traveling together: "Exert yourselves to overturn delusion and return to your original home."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the West.
Along every single golden-rope boundary path, there are billions upon billions of precious trees of exquisite joy.
The youths of the devas scatter fragrant flowers; bodhisattvas from other directions gather like clouds—immeasurable, boundless, and beyond calculation.
They bow their heads to Amitābha and stand with reverent poise.
The wind-chimes and trees resound throughout the void, extolling the Three Honored Ones without end.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.
Upon the Flower King Throne of Amitābha’s Original Vow, everything is fashioned from all manner of precious jewels.
Upon the stage, four canopies of precious drapes are spread; Amitābha sits alone, manifesting his true form.
This true form’s radiance pervades the entire Dharma-realm; those touched by this light find their resolve never to regress.
Contemplating him with single-minded devotion throughout the six periods of day and night, at the time of death one will experience bliss as if in samādhi.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.
The body of Amitābha Buddha pervades the entire Dharma-realm, appearing as reflections within the thoughts and minds of sentient beings.
Therefore, I exhort you to constantly observe: The true countenance arises from the mind as its manifestation;
That true countenance is a precious image seated upon a flower throne. When the mind opens, one beholds the adornments of that land:
Precious trees fill it, and the flowers of the three bodies are everywhere. The sound of wind-chimes and music is identical to the written text.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the West.
The body of Amitābha is the color of a golden mountain; his marks and signs, and his radiance, illuminate the ten directions.
Only those who mindfully recite the Buddha’s name shall receive his light and protection; know that his Original Vow is most powerful.
The Tathāgatas of the ten directions extend their tongues as witnesses: by single-mindedly invoking the Name, one reaches the Western Land.
There, upon the lotus pedestal, one hears the wondrous Dharma, and the vows and practices of the ten stages naturally manifest.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.
To Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, the Greatly Compassionate One, who has already attained enlightenment yet relinquishes its realization out of compassion.
Within the bodies of all beings throughout the five realms of existence, you observe the three spheres at the six periods of the day;
manifesting a body with purple-gold light, your marks and signs and majestic deportment are infinite.
Constantly extending the hands of the King of Light from ten billion worlds, you universally receive those with karmic affinity and lead them back to the Original Land.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.
The Bodhisattva Śrīkūṭa is inconceivable; his majestic radiance shines everywhere without limit.
Sentient beings with whom there is a karmic connection, touched by this light, Increase their wisdom and transcend the three realms;

the Dharma-realm trembles like a tumbleweed. Transformation Buddhas gather like clouds, filling the void, Universally exhorting those with connections to constantly maintain mindfulness, Forever severing the womb-birth and realizing the six supernormal powers.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the West.
Sitting upright in the full lotus posture, I enter samādhi; I visualize my mind, riding upon mindfulness, arriving in the West.
Behold the realm of Amitābha’s Sukhāvatī, Adorned with the seven treasures upon the earth and in the void.

The body of Amitābha is infinitely vast in measure, Yet he repeatedly exhorts sentient beings to contemplate his smaller form, Manifesting at will as sixteen or eight feet tall according to their capacities; The halo and emanated Buddhas are equal to the Original True Body before them.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.
Those of the highest grade, the highest practice, and the highest capacity seek birth in the Pure Land by severing greed and anger.
According to the distinctions in practice, there are three grades; through the five gates, one continues to assist the three causes.
Whether for one day or seven days, one applies oneself with diligent vigor. Until the end of life, one ascends the platform to emerge from the six sense-dusts.
How joyful it is to have now encountered that which is so difficult to meet! One shall forever realize the unconditioned Dharma-nature body.
Vowing to be reborn together with all sentient beings in the Land of Peace and Bliss,
I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the West.
For those of middling capacity who practice the middle path of the middle grade of rebirth, they observe the fast and precepts for one day and dwell upon a golden lotus.
Teaching filial piety toward one’s parents and dedicating merit, He explains for them the causes of happiness in the Western Land.
The Buddha and the assembly of śrāvakas come to receive him, Leading him directly to the side of Amitābha’s flower throne.
After seven days within a casket of a hundred jewels, The three grades of lotuses open, and he realizes the Lesser Truth.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the West.

Even those of the lowest grade, the lowest conduct, and the lowest faculties—including those who have committed the ten evil deeds, the five heinous crimes, and are possessed by greed and hatred—[may attain rebirth].
Having committed the four grave offenses, stolen from the Sangha, and slandered the True Dharma, one never felt shame or regret for these prior transgressions.
At the time of death, all signs of suffering gather like clouds before the person, and the fierce fires of hell suddenly appear before them.
Yet, if they encounter a spiritual friend who encourages them to single-mindedly recite the name of that Buddha, they shall attain rebirth.
The manifested Buddhas and Bodhisattvas arrive at the sound of one's voice; with a single thought, one inclines the heart and enters the precious lotus.
Though the obstacles of the three karmas have been heavy for many kalpas, it is only now that the cause of bodhicitta is first produced.
May all sentient beings together aspire to be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to the Buddha Amitābha of the Western Quarter.
The boundless bodhisattvas are my fellow students; The Tathāgata Sea of Nature is my teacher in every way.
Thirsting for the nectar of Prajñā beyond thought, I contemplate the food of non-arising to sever all hunger.
All adornments proclaim the Dharma; Without a mind to receive, one knows naturally.
Entering at will the flower-pools of the seven factors of enlightenment, The eight classes of noble ones concentrate their spirits at a single branch.
Bathed in the water of Amitābha’s heart, One is clothed in the robes of Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
